summary.one_liner: A curated, categorized list of projects that use or improve OpenStreetMap data, including editors, tools, maps, libraries, APIs and communities.
summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome" list rather than a single program. It links to OpenStreetMap-related projects grouped into sections such as editors (web, mobile, native), tools (web, mobile, native, browser extensions), changeset tools, tasking managers, maps (web, mobile, generators, styles, games), libraries by language (C/C++, JavaScript, Python, Java), public APIs and data dumps, videos, learning resources, and communities. Each entry has a one-line description and links to source code or wiki pages where available. Some entries are marked as self-hosted only, and some projects are noted as unmaintained in a separate list.
use_cases: finding an OpenStreetMap editor for web, phone or desktop
discovering routing engines and geocoding tools for OSM data
finding APIs for querying OSM data such as Overpass or SPARQL
locating libraries for working with OSM data in Python, Java, JavaScript or C++
finding tools for reviewing suspicious OSM changesets
getting started contributing to OpenStreetMap via tasking managers
notable: Organized by category (editors, tools, maps, libraries, APIs) with short descriptions for each entry
Covers both mobile and desktop OSM editors, plus changeset analysis tools
Lists language-specific libraries for Python, Java, JavaScript and C/C++
Includes a section on tasking managers aimed at new contributors
Notes that it is not affiliated with the OpenStreetMap Foundation
caveats: Entries are links to third-party projects, so availability, maintenance and licensing vary per project and are not verified here
The list is not self-hostable as a whole; some listed projects require self-deployment
The README does not state a license for the list itself
